title: Bombay High Court Quashes ICICI Bank's Sanction to Prosecute Chanda Kochhar
excerpt: Justice Milind Jadhav held that the RBI, not ICICI Bank's board, is the competent authority to sanction prosecution of a bank's head under the Prevention of Corruption Act, and that the bank failed to apply its mind.
body:
• The Bombay High Court on Wednesday, November 18, set aside ICICI Bank's sanction, dated May 15, 2023, to prosecute its former managing director and chief executive Chanda Kochhar in the ICICI-Videocon loan case.
  • Justice Milind N Jadhav held that the Reserve Bank of India is the sole competent authority under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 to grant such a sanction for the head of a banking company, and that the bank had completely failed to apply its mind to the material before it.
  • The court also quashed all consequential actions taken by the special CBI court against Kochhar, and declined the CBI's request for an eight-week stay of the judgment so it could challenge the ruling in the Supreme Court.
  • The ruling decides the validity of the sanction, not the merits of the case: the CBI's allegations over a Rs 3,250 crore loan to the Videocon Group remain allegations that have not been tested at trial.

The Bombay High Court on Wednesday set aside the sanction granted by ICICI Bank's board to prosecute its former managing director and chief executive officer Chanda Kochhar in the Videocon-ICICI Bank loan case, holding that the bank was not the authority competent in law to grant it.

Justice Milind N Jadhav, allowing Kochhar's petition in Chanda Kochhar v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., held that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the sole competent authority under law to remove the head of a banking company and to grant prosecution sanction under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. Consequently, the court also quashed all consequential actions taken by the Special Court for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) against Kochhar in the corruption case, Bar and Bench reported.

Why the sanction fell

The court found the sanction defective on two grounds: the authority that granted it was not competent to do so, and it failed to apply its mind to the material placed before it. The sanction had followed a resolution adopted by ICICI Bank's board on April 22, 2023, and the CBI informed a special court in June 2023 that the bank had approved the prosecution.

"The sanction dated 15/05/2023 under challenge is illegal and deserves to be set aside on the ground that the authority that granted the same is not a competent authority and it completely failed to apply its mind to the material, or lack thereof, placed before it while granting sanction, thereby warranting interference of this Court."

— Justice Milind N Jadhav, Bombay High Court

Kochhar had argued that the bank did not follow proper procedure while granting the sanction. Her counsel also alleged that the bank had not suffered any loss, according to Bar and Bench. A sanction under Section 19 is mandatory before a person treated as a public servant — as a bank employee is for this purpose — can be prosecuted under the Prevention of Corruption Act, The Hindu BusinessLine noted.

What the case is about

The case concerns a Rs 3,250 crore loan granted by ICICI Bank to the Videocon Group in 2012, when the bank was headed by Kochhar. The CBI has alleged cheating and irregularities in the grant of the loan. According to the agency, Kochhar cleared the loan to the Videocon Group of companies because her husband and family stood to benefit from the dealings; as a quid pro quo, her husband's company Nu Renewable allegedly received investment from Videocon. The loan later turned into a non-performing asset and was termed a bank fraud. These are the CBI's allegations; Wednesday's ruling does not decide whether they are true.

How the case reached this point

The CBI arrested Chanda Kochhar and her husband Deepak Kochhar in the case in December 2022. On January 9, 2023, the High Court ordered their release on interim bail, holding that their arrest did not satisfy the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The CBI filed a chargesheet against them in July 2023, after informing the special court in June 2023 that ICICI Bank had granted sanction to prosecute Chanda Kochhar, saying there appeared to be a quid pro quo in the loan given to Videocon.

What happens next

The CBI asked the court for an eight-week stay on the judgment so it could challenge it before the Supreme Court. Justice Jadhav declined the request, so the quashing of the sanction takes effect without that delay. Senior advocate Abad Ponda appeared for Kochhar, and Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh appeared for the CBI, Bar and Bench reported.
